old_caption: The video captures a controlled burn on a grassy hillside. The fire actively spreads across the dry, brown grass, creating a vivid contrast against the blue sky. In the foreground, a person in a yellow safety vest walks toward the fire, likely a firefighter or burn manager. The camera angle suggests it is mounted on the head of another individual, providing a first-person perspective. As the video progresses, the fire continues to advance, consuming more of the grass. Several other individuals, also in yellow vests, are scattered across the hill, some standing still while others appear to be moving, possibly managing the burn or observing its progress. A wooden structure, possibly a viewing platform, is visible in the background. The sky remains clear and bright throughout, indicating favorable weather conditions for the burn. The overall atmosphere is one of controlled activity, with the fire being managed rather than uncontrolled.
original_wisa_caption:
The video captures a dramatic scene of a controlled burn on a grassy hillside. The fire is actively spreading across the dry, brown grass, creating a vivid contrast against the blue sky. In the foreground, a person wearing a yellow safety vest is seen walking towards the fire, likely a firefighter or a burn manager. The camera angle suggests it is mounted on the head of another individual, providing a first-person perspective.

As the video progresses, the fire continues to advance, consuming more of the grass. Several other individuals, also wearing yellow vests, can be seen scattered across the hill, some standing still while others appear to be moving, possibly managing the burn or observing its progress. A wooden structure, possibly a viewing platform or part of a fire station, is visible in the background, adding context to the location.

The sky remains clear and bright throughout the video, indicating favorable weather conditions for the burn. The overall atmosphere is one of controlled activity, with the fire being managed rather than uncontrolled
caption: The video captures a dry golden hillside where a curved line of flame is already burning across the slope, its front creeping slowly through the tall grass and leaving a band of blackened, charred earth behind it. A separate foreground flame band flickers continuously along the lower edge, staying active throughout. The fire advances gradually rather than erupting, consuming the pale vegetation as it moves across the open ground. A single crew member in a yellow helmet stands on the mid-slope near the flames, drifting rightward as the camera shifts, and remains visible throughout. Several silhouetted figures hold roughly fixed positions along the upper ridge and on the elevated wooden boardwalk at the right, yet slide within the view. The camera pans and tilts gradually, drawing the platform toward the right edge while more of the left ridge and sky enter view. A dark, out-of-focus object at the right edge and a hazy smudge at the lower-right stay fixed relative to the camera, consistent with a helmet-mounted camera obstruction. The scene is viewed through this shifting perspective.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

Return JSON {"decision":"keep|edit", "issues":[{"quote":"exact span in candidate caption",
"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.
